subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: Should an explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` always fail startup when no usable Tailscale address is available, or is loopback fallback an intentional supported compatibility behavior?
rationale: The documentation implies strict tailnet binding, but changing a potentially shipped startup fallback affects availability and the gateway trust boundary; maintainer intent is needed before selecting unconditional fatal behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit Tailnet Binding
options.body: Treat inability to resolve or bind a Tailscale address as a startup error with an actionable message, while leaving automatic bind selection unchanged.

options.title: Retain Documented Fallback
options.body: Keep loopback fallback only if it is an intentional supported contract, then document it clearly and prove that authentication and operator diagnostics remain safe.

recommendation.title: Fail Explicit Tailnet Binding
recommendation.body: Treat inability to resolve or bind a Tailscale address as a startup error with an actionable message, while leaving automatic bind selection unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway remote-access documentation history makes this the best available routing candidate, though direct listener ownership remains uncertain.
